title: Probabilistic machine learning and generative models
stage: Graduate study and research in machine learning
audience: a graduate preparing for research in machine learning, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD or a research role
purpose: Learn the probabilistic view of machine learning and the generative models built on it: Bayesian linear regression and Gaussian processes, variational inference and the evidence lower bound, variational autoencoders, autoregressive models, normalizing flows, generative adversarial networks, diffusion and score-based models, energy-based models, evaluating generative models, and the uses and risks of generated media.
primary_reading: Probabilistic Machine Learning: Advanced Topics by Kevin Murphy (free PDF)

weeks.3: Variational inference and the evidence lower bound
weeks.6: Normalizing flows and the change-of-variables formula
weeks.8: Diffusion models: the forward and reverse processes
weeks.12: Generated media: uses, risks and provenance

blocks.deliverable: Compute a Gaussian process posterior from a few observations.
Derive the ELBO and compute it for a small example.
Compute the density of a transformed random variable.
Week 7 midterm; simulate a forward diffusion process.
Compute the score function of a Gaussian mixture.
Compare two evaluation metrics on supplied samples.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Generative model study: implement a one- or two-dimensional generative model of your choice (a Gaussian mixture fitted by EM, a simple flow, or a toy diffusion model) for a supplied data set, compare its samples with the data using two metrics, and write a short paper-style report with method, results, limitations and a statement on responsible use.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
